relevance_note: The paper describes 34 identifiable patients with germline TNFAIP3 variants and an HA20 diagnosis, giving per-patient variants ('a cohort of 34 individuals with HA20, 19 thereof as part of six affected families (table S1)').
method_note: All cells were read and typed from the paper; no script transcribed values. Because no code execution was available in this route, whole Table S1 row strings (which contain irregular runs of spaces) were avoided as spans; cell-level quotes (patient label, variant tokens, relation words) and sentence fragments were used instead. Scope: Table S1 describes 34 patients with germline TNFAIP3 variants (HA20-1 to HA20-34); all 34 get rows. Patients of the lymphoma cohorts (Table S2: ABC-DLBCL-*, SS-*) get no rows: their TNFAIP3 variants are tumour-tissue (somatic) findings and they belong to other cohorts. The healthy individuals (24-year-old male, 52-year-old female, 62-year-old male) are not relatives of an in-scope person and get no rows. Contradiction found: the text names 'two patients with HA20 (HA20-1 and HA20-21, 7691 cells)' for the PBMC single-cell dataset while Fig. 6C says 'HA20-1: 1454 cells; HA20-34: 6237 cells' (1454+6237 = 7691); the affected individual of that dataset is therefore ambiguous. Table S1 prints family 'none' for HA20-1 to HA20-15; this is recorded as 'not reported' in family_label_in_paper so that these 15 unrelated patients are not merged into one family. Sex of the family members is taken from the paper's own relation cells (Daughter, Son, Brother, Father, Paternal Grandmother, Granddaughter) and of HA20-1 and HA20-14 from 'her'/'his' in the text. Zygosity 'heterozygous' for all 34 variants comes from the abstract's statement about the named group that includes them ('In a cohort of 34 patients with HA20, we show that heterozygous TNFAIP3 loss ...'). Variant class is not reported except for HA20-15, where the text states 'a chromosomal deletion in 6q23.3, which encompasses TNFAIP3'. Inheritance is not reported for anyone: Table S1 lists relatives carrying the same variant but never states a parent-child transmission, and D-24 forbids inferring inheritance from pedigree information. HA20-14's additional somatic TNFAIP3 c.1880_1881delGT and MYD88 c.617C > G mutations are not recorded (tumour tissue). No stacked (' / ') table cells occur in this paper. The sentence 'Functional information of already published TNFAIP3 mutations from HA20 families can be obtained from the Infevers database' was not treated as a statement that the study's patients were described in an earlier publication. Checklist items were left 'not reported' for all 34 patients, including 'lymphoproliferation or lymphadenopathy' for the two patients with lymphoma and 'elevated inflammatory markers (CRP/ESR)' for HA20-1, whose cytokine elevation is recorded only in phenotypic_features.
